subject: Regulatory hosting qualification — hosting model, networking constraints, and MAP
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@healthsys.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Shah <arjun.shah@healthsys.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up from today — regulatory constraints and hosting options

Thanks again for walking through Redwood’s hosting options today. Quick summary from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can brief procurement/security next week: 

Highlights from call (high level)
- Primary driver: regulatory/data residency. Patient data must remain in US region and be logically separated per hospital network.
- Preferred model: private deployment (VPC or on-prem) — our security team will trade off latency vs full air-gap.
- No outbound internet egress from the inference hosts except to an allowlisted control plane IP range for management.
- KMS/HSM integration required for key custody.
- SOC 2 + HIPAA attestation required in onboarding artifacts.

Questions we promised to surface to security/procurement: 
1) Does Redwood support an air-gapped on-prem package with offline model transfer and no control-plane egress? If not fully air-gapped, what minimal control-plane egress is required (IP ranges, ports, protocols)?
2) What are the default data retention and audit-log export capabilities for private deployments?
3) Network requirements: CIDR ranges for host allowlisting, port ranges for gRPC/HTTP, and firewall NAT expectations.
4) Estimated timeline and cost buckets for Dedicated vs Private on-prem evaluation.

We have a first procurement checkpoint on Dec 10. If you can send a short one-page summary + a network topology template we can fill and return, that would be great.

-Elena
Elena Park
Head of Cloud Security, HealthSys Medical
elena.park@healthsys.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@healthsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — regulatory constraints and hosting options

Thanks Elena — great to meet you and Arjun on the call. Below is a concise recap plus the items we promised to deliver so you can share with procurement/security. I’ve attached a one-page primer and a blank network-topology template for your network team to populate.

Recap (short)
- Preferred direction: Private deployment inside your VPC (we also support an on-prem appliance for fully air-gapped setups).
- Management/control plane: can be configured to use a narrow allowlist of IP ranges; truly air-gapped on-prem is supported but requires an offline onboarding flow and an on-site install runbook.
- KMS: we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, AWS CloudHSM, and common HSM vendors).
- Compliance: we provide SOC 2 artifacts and a HIPAA addendum; we also surface audit logs and per-request metadata for retention/export.

Answers to your explicit questions
1) Air-gapped on-prem: supported. Offline model transfer supported via signed model bundles and manual import. Control-plane-less operation is possible for inference runtime; optional local telemetry upload windows can be scheduled by your ops team.
2) Retention & audit logs: configurable retention windows (30/90/365d) and export via s3-compatible endpoints or secure file transfer. Audit logs include per-request routing, model version, and token counts.
3) Network requirements (summary):
   - Control plane allowlist: specific IP ranges (we will provide a /24 set for staging and /24 for prod).
   - Inference hosts: outbound HTTPS to control plane (optional for air-gapped) and inbound gRPC/HTTP on TCP 8080/8443 (configurable).
   - KV/cache sync (if using multi-host): TCP 6379 (or custom) between hosts on private network.
   - We will provide a one-page network matrix — see attached template.
4) Timeline & cost:
   - VPC Private (managed): POC in ~4–6 weeks, GA in 8–12 weeks depending on data residency approvals.
   - On-prem air-gap: POC in 6–10 weeks, longer procurement and SOW cadence; we’ll need on-site install and security scanning windows.

Attachments: network-topology-template.pdf, redwood-deployment-primer.pdf

Next steps (proposed)
- You: populate the topology template and return (target Nov 30).
- Us: share a draft mutual-action-plan (MAP) and DocuSign-ready SOW for procurement review by Dec 6.
- Quick follow-up call to review filled topology + security checklist (30m) — suggested: Dec 2 or Dec 4.

If that aligns I’ll loop in our Solutions Engineering lead to schedule the follow-up and start the MAP.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0123

From: Elena Park <elena.park@healthsys.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Shah <arjun.shah@healthsys.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 20:41:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — regulatory constraints and hosting options

Vivek — thanks for the clear summary. Attached is our filled network topology overview (HealthSys_network_overview.pdf) and short answers to a few items from our security team: 

- We prefer a managed private VPC model for the initial POC; if that meets their constraints we will evaluate the on-prem appliance for production.
- On egress: the security team will only allow control-plane egress to predefined IPs; we will need your exact IP list and periodic rotation procedures.
- KMS: AWS KMS preferred; we will require key rotation policies and key-splitting controls.
- Timeline: procurement internal approval target Dec 10; legal prefers a single SOW covering POC + follow-on reserved capacity.

Procurement asks
- Please provide a short MAP (Gantt-style) with deliverables, owners, and gating criteria (security sign-off, network testing, model transfer).
- Provide a sample SOW template and your standard on-prem runbook so we can review with operations.

We can do a 30m sync on Dec 3 (10:00–10:30 PT) to walk the filled topology and finalize the MAP.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Attachment: HealthSys_network_overview.pdf

Appended here with the quick mutual action plan we discussed on the sync (Dec 3). Thanks for sending the filled topology — that made the call very productive. 

Short MAP (deliverables & owners)
- 2026-12-03: MAP draft (Redwood) — owner: Vivek — attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx
- 2026-12-06: Provide allowlist IPs + rotation procedure (Redwood) — owner: Ben Carter
- 2026-12-08: Security checklist & sample SOW (Redwood legal/solutions) — owner: Marissa Cole
- 2026-12-10: Procurement decision checkpoint (HealthSys) — owner: Elena/Arjun
- 2027-01-10: Target POC kickoff (if procurement approved) — owners: joint

Technical constraints/notes (call highlights)
- Air-gap option: will require manual signed model bundles and a secure USB transfer process defined in the runbook.
- Minimal control-plane egress: we can operate with a narrow window for telemetry uploads; we will also support a fully offline mode (longer onboarding & patch cadence).
- KMS/HSM: we will support AWS KMS + CloudHSM and can provide an HSM integration guide for your ops team.

Immediate next steps (this week)
1) Ben: publish the prod allowlist IPs and port matrix (by Dec 6).
2) Marissa: circulate a draft SOW and on-prem runbook for review (by Dec 8).
3) HealthSys: confirm procurement checkpoint participants and share any leather-bound security questionnaire (if any) by Dec 7.

I’ve attached the MAP and a short deployment primer. Once legal gives thumbs-up we’ll convert the MAP to a DocuSign-ready SOW and route to your procurement contact.
